items.text: Asks how the service sheds load when Payments or Fulfillment slows down, what is rejected first, and how pending work is bounded.
Requests an explicit service-to-service authorization matrix and a test that prevents a caller from substituting an arbitrary customer identity.
Checks that configuration, database credentials, and provider settings are injected at runtime rather than coupled to the service artifact.
Asks for a versioned contract and deprecation window for callers that continue to use the adapter, including how incompatible changes are detected.
Requests evidence that a zone loss, dependency outage, or worker backlog stays within the availability objective and has a bounded recovery path.
Asks who owns the public SLO and error-budget decision when rollout signals disagree across regions or callers.

weakAnswers: The proposal is clear and the staged rollout looks sensible.
Consider scalability, monitoring, and future growth before implementation.
The service boundary and API design seem reasonable; add more tests.
The document covers performance, reliability, security, and operations well.
